Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed, homogeneous mass in the right upper lung zone without obvious signs of adjacent vessel invasion or pleural effusion. This radiographic appearance—a sharply defined, non-invasive mass—is characteristic of Pleuropulmonary Synovial Sarcoma (PPSS), distinguishing it from more invasive primary lung cancers or heterogeneous masses.
